elements_not_encoded.text: Give continuous cycles of 30 chest compressions and 2 breaths with bag-valve-mask attached to 100% oxygen at 10-15L/min.
Attach monitor/defibrillator and pause compressions to check initial heart rhythm:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm check routes to shock/no-shock management; no triage or diagnosis output on this page.

elements_not_encoded.text: Ventricular fibrillation (VF)
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm branch (VF) leads only to defibrillation management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia (pVT)
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm branch (pVT) leads only to defibrillation management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Asystole
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm branch (asystole) leads only to CPR/adrenaline management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Any other rhythm:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm branch (other rhythm) leads to pulse check and CPR management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)
elements_not_encoded.reason: Rhythm branch (PEA) leads only to CPR/adrenaline management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Give shock of 120-150J.
If monophasic defibrillator, give instead shock of 360J.
Immediately restart CPR, starting with chest compressions.

elements_not_encoded.text: Doctor to consider intubation. If intubated, give 1 breath every 6 seconds and continuous chest compressions.
Look for and manage possible cause:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Lead-in to the cause list; the 'likely' diagnoses within it are encoded from their own elements.

elements_not_encoded.text: If trauma, diarrhoea/vomiting or dehydration2, give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly. Repeat if needed. If unsure, discuss with doctor.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Fluid resuscitation for trauma/diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration; the dehydration definition (footnote 2) is encoded from the footnote element.

elements_not_encoded.text: If glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) or unable to measure 19. If temperature ≤ 35°C 18. If overdose/poisoning, discuss with specialist or poison helpline 200.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Glucose -> page 19, temperature -> page 18, overdose/poisoning -> specialist/poison helpline page 200; no triage logic here.

elements_not_encoded.text: Decide when to stop CPR
elements_not_encoded.reason: Section header for decisions about stopping CPR (management).

elements_not_encoded.text: How to give chest compressions
If ongoing VF/pVT, temperature ≤ 35°C, snake bite or overdose/poisoning, continue CPR and discuss/transfer urgently.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Decision to continue CPR and transfer; the patient is already Emergency.

elements_not_encoded.text: Ensure patient is lying on firm surface. If on bed, use backboard or move patient onto floor.
Place heel of one hand over lower half of sternum. Place heel of second hand on top of first hand.
If none of above or asystole after 20 minutes of continuous CPR or incurable underlying disease, consider stopping CPR in consultation with doctor.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Decision to stop CPR; not a triage or diagnosis output.

elements_not_encoded.text: Push down quickly, hard (depth of 5-6cm) and fast (100-120 per minute).
Allow chest to return to normal shape between compressions.
If CPR stopped, pronounce dead and arrange bereavement counselling for family.
Do not interrupt compressions unless giving ventilations or checking heart rhythm.
Swop with colleague every 2 minutes to avoid fatigue.

judgment_calls.decision: Due_to is (or Cardiac arrest, Absent pulse): Cardiac arrest is the adult Emergency warning sign; Absent pulse is the page's literal 'no pulse'.
Probable Dehydration if there is no pulse and any of thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor or BP < 90/60.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Leave the footnote unencoded as a note; require all signs; leave it unscoped by no pulse (a global dehydration definition).

judgment_calls.decision: Not encoded: they route only to defibrillation/adrenaline management, which is out of scope.
judgment_calls.alternatives: check_for the rhythms and use them in an Emergency priority rule (redundant with no pulse).

judgment_calls.decision: Emergency for no pulse/cardiac arrest (CPR is an explicit escalation in Will's briefing).
'Thirst' (footnote 2, a dehydration sign) encoded as 'Thirst due to water deprivation' (finding), the term VHA's vocabulary already uses.
judgment_calls.alternatives: 'Increased thirst' (finding), a sibling under 'Thirst finding' that does not presume a cause; the grouper 'Thirst finding' (includes normal/reduced thirst).
